talks.title: Expo West 2024: BUILDING HEALTHY AND HIGH-PERFORMING TECH TEAMS PANEL
talks.teaser: Expo West 2024: BUILDING HEALTHY AND HIGH-PERFORMING TECH TEAMS PANEL.
talks.summary:
Overview: A panel at Expo West discusses building healthy, high-performing technology teams, exploring leadership challenges in diverse, distributed engineering organizations across global technology companies.

Key Topics: Balancing productivity with team wellbeing; cross-cultural communication challenges referenced via Erin Meyer's Culture Map framework; managing diverse team expectations across time zones; and harmonizing competing business requirements with employee needs.

Technical Details: Panelists from Amazon and other technology organizations share experiences managing globally distributed teams with varying cultural communication styles. They emphasize that leadership success depends on communication quality and cultural awareness across boundaries.

Takeaways: High-performing tech teams require intentional culture-building and cross-cultural communication skills. Leaders must understand how cultural backgrounds shape team dynamics, expectations, and productivity patterns.

talks.title: Expo West 2024: BATTLING THROUGH BAD DATA: HOW TO SUCCEED IN AI
talks.teaser: Expo West 2024: BATTLING THROUGH BAD DATA: HOW TO SUCCEED IN AI.
talks.summary:
Why AI Projects Fail

Dr Janet Bastman, Napier AI chief data scientist, opens with a rhetorical question about money wasted on doomed AI efforts. She cites Memorial Sloan Kettering’s IBM Watson cancer project—launched with fanfare, scrapped by 2018 after doctors called recommendations unsafe, costing about $62 million over six years as a cautionary example.

Rejecting Magic-Box Thinking

Bastman contrasts vendor hype—gather data, feed AI, get answers—with data science discipline. She argues science is magic that works, and that niche medical summarization remains hard even for modern LLMs. Failed projects often skip user feedback, doctor validation, and iterative checks.

Defining and Fixing Bad Data

Bad data means information unfit for purpose: inconsistent, unbalanced, inaccurate, or unrepresentative samples that mislead models. Bastman urges applying scientific principles—clear problem definition, representative sampling, and honest assessment of whether datasets support confident answers—before scaling investment.

talks.title: Expo West 2024: HOW THE INTELLIGENCE REVOLUTION CAN DRIVE SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT
talks.teaser: Expo West 2024: HOW THE INTELLIGENCE REVOLUTION CAN DRIVE SOCIO-ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT.
talks.summary:
Planetary Stakes

NVIDIA senior scientist Allison Bishop opens with Rockström’s nine planetary boundaries, noting two-thirds are already breached. She ties climate harm to geopolitical oil dependence and argues visualization helps non-experts grasp risks and fund resilience.

Climate Visualization for Vulnerable Nations

At COP28 NVIDIA supported BOSS (Big Ocean Sustainable States) nations facing sea-level rise. Partners like RSS-Hydro use GPU tools to render physically accurate 3D scenarios—e.g., Tonga inundation by 2150—from elevation models, making abstract pledges tangible for policymakers.

Digital Twins and Mission-Critical AI

Examples include Cesium/Maxar digital twins of Cape Canaveral synced with live telemetry for launch safety, AV training in Omniverse metaverse environments, and Earth-2 climate/weather simulation. AI emulates physics to cut compute orders of magnitude while serving billion-user decision platforms.

Efficiency and Accessible Forecasting

NVIDIA highlights Green500 leadership and UK Isambard 3 Grace-Hopper systems. Models like CorrDiff downscale coarse climate data cheaply; ForecastNet demos show eight-line Python weather inference. Bishop credits gaming-driven GPU evolution now applied to humanitarian and planetary stewardship.

talks.title: Expo West 2024: EMBRACING TRANSFORMATIONAL LEADERSHIP
talks.teaser: Expo West 2024: EMBRACING TRANSFORMATIONAL LEADERSHIP.
talks.summary:
Leadership transformation

Ir Thompson John, JP Morgan Chase equities technology transformation executive, uses Satya Nadella's experience raising a son with cerebral palsy to illustrate how personal adversity can reshape corporate empathy, accessibility investment, and inclusive hiring at Microsoft after 2014.

From command to purpose

She contrasts command-and-control management with transformational leadership: emotional intelligence, feedback-seeking, purpose beyond bottom line, paid parental leave expansion, psychological safety to fail fast, and diversity of thinking as an innovation driver supported by research.

Collective intelligence

Drawing on agile mindset rather than tools alone, she advocates collective estimation, continuous collaboration, and tapping human plus machine intelligence across a two-thousand-person global organization. Leaders, she argues, can influence society beyond the firm by embedding CSR values such as those emphasized during Chase UK rollout.

talks.title: Expo West 2024: THE KEY TRENDS SHAPING THE FUTURE OF INFRASTRUCTURE
talks.teaser: Expo West 2024: THE KEY TRENDS SHAPING THE FUTURE OF INFRASTRUCTURE.
talks.summary:
## Overview
Arm's Cheryl Hung surveys infrastructure trends at Digit Expo West—from cloud-native maturity to AI engineering.

## Cloud-Native Divide
CNCF survey data shows beginners struggle with training and expertise, while mature cloud-native shops report security and complexity as top challenges—tooling proliferation hasn't simplified operations.

## Cloud-Native AI
Hung describes leveraging datacenter CPU/GPU capacity for AI workloads and the emergence of dedicated ML/AI engineer roles blending data science with infrastructure skills.

## Recommendations
She urges education so users understand AI they consume, and participation in communities like Linux Foundation AI/data and CNCF groups to track fast-moving standards.

## Takeaways
Infrastructure's next decade pairs cloud-native operations with AI scale—security and skills gaps remain the binding constraints.
